t.5.55.2: The sky-ocean, whose great fish was Punarvasu, whose great seizing monster was Lohitāṅga, whose great island was Airāvata, and which was stirred by Svāti as by a swan.
t.5.55.1: The lovely sky, with the moon for its white water-lily and the sun for its kāraṇḍava duck, splendid, with the stars Tiṣya and Śravaṇa for its flock of geese and the clouds for its moss and grassy banks.
t.5.55.4: As if devouring the sky, as if scratching the lord of the stars, as if carrying off the heavens together with the constellations and the orb of the sun,
t.5.55.3: That sky-ocean, whose waves arose from masses of wind, whose waters were cool with the rays of the moon, and whose blossoming lotuses and water-lilies were the serpents, Yakṣas and Gandharvas.
t.5.55.5: The glorious and mighty monkey Hanūmān, ranging through the sky, goes toward the abode of the wind, as if dragging along masses of clouds.
t.5.55.6: Great clouds shone forth, some pale white and ruddy in hue, some dark blue and madder-red, and others green and ruddy in colour.
t.5.55.7: Entering the masses of clouds and emerging again and again, now hidden and now visible, he appears like the moon.
t.5.55.8: Roaring with a mighty roar, his great cry like the thunder of clouds, the one of great splendour came back again across the ocean by its middle course.
t.5.55.9: Having touched Sunābha, the lord of mountains, the mighty one came on with great speed, like an iron arrow loosed from the bowstring.
t.5.55.10: Having drawn somewhat near, that bull among monkeys beheld the great mountain, which resembled a mighty cloud of Mahendra, and he roared aloud.
t.5.55.11: Hearing the roar of him who was roaring, those monkeys on every side all became eager, longing to see their friend.
t.5.55.12: Then Jāmbavān, that foremost of monkeys, his mind thrilled with joy, addressed all the monkeys and spoke these words.
t.5.55.13: That Hanūmān has surely accomplished his task in every way; of this there is no doubt. For had he not accomplished his task, his roar would not be of this kind.
t.5.55.14: Perceiving the rushing speed of the great-souled one's arms and thighs and hearing his roar, the monkeys, overjoyed, sprang up here and there.
t.5.55.15: Overjoyed and eager to see Hanūmān, they leapt from treetop to treetop and from peak to peak.
t.5.55.17: Seeing that great monkey, who resembled a mass of dense clouds, swooping down toward them, all the vānaras then stood with palms joined in reverence.
t.5.55.16: Delighted, the vānaras seized the richly blossoming branches at the tops of the trees and waved them about like bright garments.
t.5.55.18: Then the swift monkey, huge as a mountain, came down upon the peak of that mountain Mahendra, which was thick with trees.
t.5.55.19: Then all those foremost of the vānaras, their hearts filled with joy, surrounded the great-souled Hanūmān and stood by him in attendance.
t.5.55.20: And all of them, surrounding him who had come back unharmed, were filled with the highest joy, all of them with beaming faces.
t.5.55.21: Taking up gifts, along with roots and fruits, the monkeys honored in return the son of Māruta, the best of monkeys.
t.5.55.22: Some, delighted, roared aloud and likewise raised joyful shouts of "kilakilā"; and the bull-like monkeys, thrilled with joy, brought branches of trees.
t.5.55.23: Then Hanumān, that great monkey, paid reverence to his elders and venerable ones, headed by Jāmbavān, and also to the prince Aṅgada.
t.5.55.24: Honored by those two and gratified by the monkeys, the worthy and valiant one reported in brief: "The queen has been seen."
t.5.55.25: Then, taking the son of Vālin by the hand, he sat down in a delightful woodland spot of Mount Mahendra.
t.5.55.26: Then Hanumān, delighted, said to those bulls among the monkeys: "She, the daughter of Janaka, has been seen, dwelling in the Aśoka grove."
t.5.55.27: The blameless young woman, guarded by exceedingly dreadful rākṣasīs, wearing her hair in a single braid and longing for the sight of Rāma, is worn out by fasting, soiled, with matted hair, and emaciated.
t.5.55.28: Then, hearing from Māruti the words "She has been seen," words of great import and like nectar, all the monkeys became joyful.
t.5.55.29: Some of the mighty ones hissed, others roared, others thundered; some raised cries of joy, and still others roared back in answer.
t.5.55.30: Some of the elephant-like monkeys, overjoyed, raised their tails high and lashed about with their long tails, curved and stretched out.
t.5.55.31: But other monkeys, filled with delight, leapt down from the mountain peaks and touched Hanūmān, who was like an elephant.
t.5.55.32: Then, in the midst of all the monkey heroes, Aṅgada addressed these unsurpassed words to Hanūmān, who had finished speaking.
t.5.55.33: O monkey, there is no one to be found equal to you in strength and valour, since you have leapt across the vast ocean and come back again.
t.5.55.34: By good fortune the glorious queen, Rāma's wife, has been seen by you; by good fortune Kākutstha will cast off the grief born of his separation from Sītā.
t.5.55.35: Then the delighted monkeys, surrounding Aṅgada, Hanumān and Jāmbavān, settled upon broad rocks.
t.5.55.36: Eager to hear of the leap across the ocean and of the sight of Laṅkā, of Sītā and of Rāvaṇa, all the foremost of monkeys stood with joined palms, their faces turned up toward Hanumān's face.
t.5.55.37: There stood the glorious Aṅgada, surrounded by many vānaras, like the lord of the gods in heaven being attended upon by the gods.
t.5.55.38: Then the great and lofty mountain summit, joyfully occupied by the renowned and glorious Hanūmān and likewise by Aṅgada, whose arms were bound with armlets, became radiant with splendor.
